blocks.x: Claims-fraud network analytics on a governed lakehouse, improper-payment recovery up 34% and investigator false-positive burden down 41%
Identity withheld, a health insurer whose special-investigations unit worked referral lists that aged out before the schemes did. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline quarter measured the hunt: SIU caseload built from rule hits, 71% of which cleared on first review, while the schemes that cost the most, provider rings billing across aliases, never triggered a single rule.
Claims, provider registry and member data lived in three systems with different identifiers, so no analyst could see one provider's behavior across entities without a week of manual stitching.

We built the network layer first: one governed entity model resolving providers, facilities and billers across systems, graph analytics surfacing rings as structures, shared addresses, tax IDs, device usage patterns, and a case system where evidence assembles itself for each referral. Investigators start with the network in view, not a spreadsheet of hits.
